# manual-case-release-1.7.2308.txt -- #5703
#
# The reporter's own environment: "DXC version dxcompiler.dll: 1.7 -
# 1.7.2308.7 (69e54e290); dxil.dll: 1.7(101.7.2308.12)". This tag is
# catalogued locally (triage.db `releases` row for v1.7.2308) at:
#   <repo>/build/tools/clang/test/dxc_releases/v1.7.2308/dxc_2023_08_14/bin/x64/dxc.exe
# No stable release archive ships dxl.exe or dxa.exe (established for
# #4168's manual-case-release-tools.txt); dxl is exercised the same way
# link4168.py does it: `dxc.exe <args> -link`, which is exactly what
# tools/clang/tools/dxl/dxl.cpp does under the hood.
#
# --- as-filed source, no fix ---
# repro-as-filed.hlsl is the reporter's HLSL verbatim (numthreads only, no
# [shader("compute")] attribute).
#
# $ dxc.exe -T lib_6_3 -O3 -Fo lib-1_7_2308.dxo repro-as-filed.hlsl
#   (warning: attribute 'numthreads' ignored without accompanying shader
#   attribute [-Wmisplaced-attributes] -- same warning current main gives)
#   exit 0
# lib-1_7_2308.dxo parts: SFI0(8) RDAT(224) STAT(1728) HASH(20) DXIL(1812)
#
# $ dxc.exe -T cs_6_3 -E main -O3 -Fo linked-1_7_2308.dxo lib-1_7_2308.dxo -link
#   exit 0  (link succeeds at v1.7.2308 even without [shader("compute")] --
#   see method-notes.md; current main's dxl.exe fails to find function
#   "main" on the same as-filed source and needs the attribute added. That
#   entry-point-resolution difference is a separate, unconfirmed finding
#   and is NOT part of this issue's verdict -- it only affects whether the
#   reporter's literal source links today, not whether RDAT survives
#   linking once it does.)
# linked-1_7_2308.dxo parts: SFI0(8) ISG1(8) OSG1(8) PSV0(120) ILDN(44)
#   HASH(20) DXIL(1532)
#
# Result: identical shape to main-debug-link5703's ground-truth capture --
# RDAT present in the unlinked library, absent from the linked/finalized
# container, PSV0 present instead. This is the reporter's own build
# reproducing its own reported "actual behavior" exactly, which is the
# strongest evidence that nothing has changed since the report: the
# container format's RDAT/PSV0 split has always worked this way for a
# `Link(..., "cs_6_3", ...)` call, at least as far back as v1.7.2308
# (2023-08-14, the exact build named in the issue).
